extracted.intended_audience: EPO examiners and international patent applicants/representatives interacting with the EPO as ISA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how the EPO, acting as International Searching Authority (ISA), must conduct international searches and draft ISRs/WO-ISAs including handling of non-unity, protests, excluded subject-matter, incomplete/no-search situations, informal clarification and sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for examination in the European phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of the application in the European phase will be based on either A, B1 or C (see GL/EPO F‑V, 13.1(iii)). For the claims relating to inventions B2, B3 and D, an invitation under Rule 164(2) EPC will be issued in accordance with GL/EPO F‑V, 13.1(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates which ISR/WO‑ISA designations determine the scope of later European examination and when Rule 164(2) invitations are used for certain inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling if additional search fees not paid
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after an invitation to pay additional search fees, the applicant does not pay further fees, the file will not be returned to the examiner, but the final search report and the WO‑ISA, which were already prepared by the examiner at the initial search stage, will be sent out by the formalities officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further action by examiner; formalities officer issues the already prepared ISR and WO‑ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling if additional search fees paid without protest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has paid additional search fees without protest, a complete search will be carried out for the inventions for which search fees have been paid and the ISR will be issued for these inventions. The WO‑ISA will be drafted for the claims for which search fees have been paid. Section IV is to be filled out, and Section III must be modified to the actual payment of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must perform complete search for paid inventions and adjust ISR/WO‑ISA sections to reflect payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of additional search fees under protest triggers protest procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant pays some or all of the additional fees under protest, this triggers the protest procedure for determining whether the request for payment of the additional fees was justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment under protest initiates formal review; see GL/PCT‑EPO B‑VII, 7 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects when Review Panel finds protest fully or partly justified
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Review Panel decided that the protest was fully or partly justified, the examiner will follow the decision of the Review Panel and will proceed to establish the ISR and WO‑ISA for the inventions for which search fees have been paid. In the ISR the examiner will adapt the number of inventions and their definitions as well as the non‑unity reasoning to be consistent with the decision of the review panel. In the WO‑ISA, Section IV and the reasoning will be adapted to the decision of the Review Panel and Section III will be modified to the actual payment of fees. Under Section V an opinion as to novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability for all searched inventions will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt all parts of ISR/WO‑ISA (Sections III, IV, V and non‑unity reasoning) to match Review Panel decision; include substantive opinions for searched inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect when protest fully justified and application considered unitary
rubrics_metrics.description: In the special situation where the protest was fully justified and where, as a consequence, the application is considered unitary, the examiner will follow the decision of the Review Panel and send a final ISR with no indication of non‑unity. In Section IV of the WO‑ISA the examiner will indicate that the requirement of unity of invention is complied with and that the search report has been established in respect of all parts of the application; no reasons need to be given on the separate sheet. Under Section V, an opinion as to novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability for all claims will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final ISR and WO‑ISA must reflect unitary finding; give full opinion on all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect when protest not justified
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Review Panel decided that the protest was not justified, the examiner will follow the decision of the Review Panel and proceed to establish the ISR and the WO‑ISA for the inventions for which search fees have been paid. In the ISR and the WO‑ISA (Section IV) he will indicate that the requirement of unity is not complied with. Section III will be modified to the actual payment of fees, and under Section V an opinion as to novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability for all searched inventions will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate non‑unity and provide opinions for searched inventions; adjust Sections III and IV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest admissibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be admissible the protest should satisfy the following requirements: the applicant must have paid the additional fees (Rule 40.2(e)), and the prescribed protest fee. The payment under protest must be accompanied by a reasoned statement, i.e. the reasoned statement should have been filed with the payment or at the latest within the time limit set in Form 206. The reasoned statement must comply with Rule 40.2(c); i.e. the applicant should argue why the international application complies with/does not comply with the requirement of unity of invention or why the amount of the required additional fee is excessive. In the protest the applicant should question the number of additional fees that he has been invited to pay, and not the amount of a single additional fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirement checklist: payment of fees, protest fee, timely filed reasoned statement addressing number of fees/unity per Rule 40.2(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of formalities officer vs Review Panel in protests
rubrics_metrics.description: The payment of the protest fee and the filing of a purported reasoned statement are assessed by specially trained formalities officers. Any substantive analysis is made by the Review Panel when assessing the justification of the protest. If the applicant merely submits a statement of disagreement without reasoning, the Review Panel will refer to the reasoning contained in the invitation to pay additional search fees (Form 206) when taking its decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities officers check admissibility; Review Panel performs substantive evaluation; mere disagreement without reasons is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and scope of Review Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant pays the additional fees under protest and the protest is found admissible, the case is referred to the director to appoint a three‑member Review Panel, which comprises the examiner in charge, an examiner as chairperson of the Review Panel and a further examiner. The purpose of the Review Panel is to determine, on the basis of the protest, whether the request for payment of additional fees by the examiner was justified on the basis of the reasoning given. The review does not allow a re‑evaluation to determine possible additional grounds for lack of unity. The scope of the review is limited to those inventions for which additional fees have been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three‑member panel; limited scope — only the inventions paid for and only grounds raised in the protest are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Panel decisions and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If wholly justified the Review Panel will inform the applicant with Form 212, order the reimbursement of all the additional fees and the protest fee, and the search will be carried out for the inventions for which fees were paid. If not justified the Review Panel will communicate this using Form 212 and give reasoning; the search will be carried out for inventions paid. If partially justified the Review Panel will communicate partial justification, give reasoning, order reimbursement of the corresponding additional fees but not the protest fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 212 is used for decisions; reimbursements depend on extent of justification; searches carried out for inventions paid in all outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and consistency of final ISR/WO‑ISA with protest decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The formalities officer will send the decision of the Review Panel to the applicant and the IB. The decision on protest (Form 212) will be sent out together with the final ISR and WO‑ISA in order to ensure that both are consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the ISR/WO‑ISA content matches the Review Panel decision and that decision is distributed with the search documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences in European phase after unsuccessful protest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Review Panel confirms the initial finding of lack of unity and if the application enters the European phase with unamended claims, the Examining Division will, as a rule, confirm the lack of unity and request the applicant to limit the claims to one invention and to file (a) divisional application(s) for the other invention(s). Alternatively, the applicant may amend the claims to render them unitary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining Division usually follows Review Panel; applicant must limit claims or file divisionals or amend claims to restore unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle that declaration of no search should be exceptional
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, a declaration of no search under Art. 17(2)(a)(ii) should remain an exception. Under the PCT, even if the applicant amends the claims to overcome the objection, an additional search is not possible. Therefore, at least some effort should be made to carry out a meaningful search of at least part of the claimed subject‑matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should attempt meaningful partial searches rather than issue no‑search declarations; no subsequent PCT additional search if declaration issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject‑matter the ISA is not required to search (PCT/EPC exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject‑matter which would be excluded from patentability under the EPC (non‑technical inventions, programs for computers, methods of doing business, medical methods and the exception for plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes) is identified as subject‑matter for which the ISA and/or the IPEA is not required to carry out search and international preliminary examination. The criteria applied for the decision not to perform an international search are the same as for the European procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply EPC exclusions and the same practice as European searches; restriction should be indicated in ISR and WO‑ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and written opinion when all claims excluded from search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the subject‑matter of all claims constitutes a subject excluded from the search, a declaration of non‑establishment of the international search report is issued pursuant to Article 17(2)(a) on Form PCT/ISA/203, indicating the reasons. A written opinion is established, even though, in the absence of a search, it cannot address the questions of novelty and inventive step and may not be able to address other questions, such as industrial applicability. The written opinion should contain full reasoning as to why the search is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if no ISR is established, provide a WO‑ISA with full reasoning explaining inability to search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of medical/therapeutic/diagnostic claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims directed to medical treatment which would fall under the exceptions to patentability under Art. 53(c) EPC should, in principle, also be exempted from international search. Depending on claim wording (various types a–k), some claims may be searched and examined (e.g., 'compound X for use as a medicament' vs 'method of treatment using X') and the WO‑ISA should add a remark that novelty and inventive step have been assessed according to EPO practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow EPO practice and the table of claim types: certain use/Swiss‑type/composition claims are searchable with an EPO practice remark; method‑of‑treatment claims are generally excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer‑implemented business methods practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO as ISA will, in all cases where the subject‑matter of the international application involves technical means, consider the application and to the extent possible provide a search report for those parts of it which are more than mere business methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where technical character exists, search the technical parts; mere business methods may be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'no meaningful search' and its limited application
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'meaningful search' should be read to include a search that within reason is complete enough to determine whether the claimed invention complies with the substantive requirements, i.e. novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, and/or sufficiency, support and clarity. A finding of 'no meaningful search' should be limited to exceptional situations in which no search at all is possible for a particular claim, for example where the description, the claims or the drawings are totally unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion: attempt to search any parts that can be sufficiently understood; do not use 'reasons of economy' to justify incomplete searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples where meaningful search may be impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: Non‑limiting examples: (i) claims lacking support/insufficient disclosure (broad speculative claims supported only by limited disclosure), (ii) claims lacking conciseness (so many claims or possibilities that determining protection sought is unduly burdensome), (iii) claims lacking clarity (parameters that render comparison with prior art impossible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, restrict search to worked examples or narrower disclosed invention where appropriate; consider informal clarification before restricting search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide/amino acid sequence listing requirements and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sequence listing is not available in electronic form and/or does not comply with WIPO Standard ST.25, the EPO as ISA will invite the applicant to furnish the sequence listing in electronic text format and pay a late furnishing fee within one month. If not submitted, the EPO will either issue a declaration of no meaningful search under Art. 17(2)(a)(ii) and Rule 13ter.1(d) or issue an incomplete search report under Art. 17(2)(b) with a declaration, and otherwise carry out the search to the extent possible without the listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide compliant electronic sequence listings can lead to incomplete/no search; affects subsequent IPEA procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of informal clarification prior to issuing incomplete ISR/no search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description, claims or drawings fail to comply with a requirement to such an extent that no meaningful search can be made, the examiner may informally contact the applicant to clarify specific aspects of the application before the search is carried out. Informal clarification may take the form of a telephone consultation (minutes must be written) or a written request (Form PCT/ISA/207) sent by fax. A short time limit (normally two weeks) can be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highly recommended to invite informal clarification before issuing incomplete ISR or no search; telephone may be preferable given short PCT time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling replies to informal clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not reply within the set time limit, the examiner will prepare the search report and WO‑ISA to the extent possible without the requested clarification. If the applicant replies after the time limit and the search report has not yet been established, the reply should be taken into account; if the search report has already been established the reply will not be taken into account. If the applicant replies in time, the examiner will prepare the search report and WO‑ISA taking the reply into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely replies are incorporated; late replies only if report not yet established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and indication of restrictions in ISR and WO‑ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: A restriction of the search will not always be indicated in the ISR; often the extent of the search and reasons for restriction will only be indicated in the WO‑ISA. The opinion given is normally restricted to what has actually been searched. If only some claims/parts can be searched and no likely fallback exists, a precise indication of what has been searched with full reasoning must be entered into both the ISR and WO‑ISA and an opinion on novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability of the searched subject‑matter must be given. If a searchable fallback exists the ISR will be filled as for a complete search for those claims and the WO‑ISA must indicate what was searched and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what was searched and why; add full reasoning in WO‑ISA and ISR when applicable; opinions limited to searched subject‑matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction due to Rule 39 exceptions must be indicated in ISR
rubrics_metrics.description: A restriction of the search due to exceptions mentioned in Rule 39 (e.g. medical treatment claims) must always be indicated in the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ISR explicitly indicates Rule 39‑based restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of incomplete search and lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of unity of invention and Art. 17(2)(a)(ii) (no meaningful search) are separate requirements. However, it is possible that an application both violates clarity/disclosure/support/conciseness to such an extent that a meaningful search cannot be carried out, and lacks unity. In that case, the examiner can combine an incomplete search and a finding of non‑unity. The applicant should not be invited to pay additional fees for subject‑matter which will later not be searched under Art. 17(2)(a)(ii). Typically, a non‑unity objection could be made first and then an incomplete search applied to the searched invention. However, if the complexity lies in lack of clarity, the search will be restricted first, and the non‑unity objection applied to the clear parts of the claimed subject‑matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invite fees for subject‑matter that will be excluded from search; sequence the objections appropriately depending on whether clarity or unity drives complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple independent claims per category not per se reason for incomplete search
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple independent claims in one category are per se not a reason for an incomplete search. Generally, an opinion must be given on all searched claims. Only one independent claim in each category needs to be treated in detail; short comments would normally suffice for further independent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide opinions on all searched claims; use concise treatment for multiple independent claims; consider clarity/conciseness objections under Box VIII of WO‑ISA where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report content restrictions and types of report
rubrics_metrics.description: A search report must contain no matter, in particular no expressions of opinion, reasoning, arguments or explanations, other than that required by the Form or referred to in GL/PCT‑EPO B‑X, 9.2.8. However, this does not apply to the written opinion. The EPO as ISA will draw up different types of search reports: international search reports under the PCT and international‑type search reports. A number of different possible limitations of the scope of the search report exist (declaration instead of search under Art.17(2)(a), incomplete search under Art.17(2)(b), partial ISR due to lack of unity, incomplete due to missing sequence listings). The Search Division is responsible for drawing up the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep ISR strictly to form content; include reasoning in WO‑ISA; choose correct type of ISR/statement depending on situation (no‑search, incomplete, partial, sequence‑listing issues).
